The same entries as ard.json, at the path the AI Catalog Standard reads. Serve both: ARD crawlers read ard.json first, other agents read ai-catalog.json.

It carries no trust manifest. The AI Catalog Standard keeps trust metadata in a trustManifests array, where each manifest names its contributor and carries evidence: a signature, attestations, provenance, a trust schema or extensions. Add one when you have that evidence to publish.

Serve this file at https://debian.org/.well-known/poppy.json. As written it is a valid version 1.0 document that lets personal agents browse debian.org signed out, as long as debian.org names no OAuth issuer (see below).

Serve it from debian.org itself, without a redirect: the file speaks for the host that finally serves it, so organization.domain must name that host. If it is served from another host, such as www.debian.org, change organization.domain to that host.

Agents look for your OAuth issuer at https://debian.org/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. With no issuer at all, that URL should answer 404. If it already serves metadata, its resource must be exactly https://debian.org, and the authorization server it lists becomes your Personal Agent Protocol issuer: that server's RFC 8414 metadata must then list https://debian.org in protected_resources, and if it lists several servers, set auth.issuer to the one agents use. Otherwise agents will not use this file. If that issuer offers agents no sign-in yet, add "auth": { "disabled": true }.

To let personal agents sign in and use your APIs, publish protected resource metadata at https://debian.org/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource with resource set to https://debian.org and your OAuth issuer in authorization_servers, and list your APIs under apis, each with a type, url and description. Do this only once your issuer's RFC 8414 metadata lists https://debian.org in protected_resources and refresh_token in grant_types_supported, every listed API accepts the Personal Agent Protocol Session header and your access tokens, and each listed MCP server's protected resource metadata names its own url as the resource and your issuer in authorization_servers.
